Meta harness, planted-waste test: 3 rounds of team-meta-review cut compute per batch from 16.3 to 4.4 container minutes (3.7x less) at the same job class with the same answers; the same model with a plain instruction reached 9.8 (from 15.1). Container time with no answer: skill 83% -> 48%, plain 84% -> 73%; clean work is 10-16%. 3 runs per arm, 9 review runs per arm (claude-opus-5-5), 6 planted inefficiencies in a CPU study on the stored MATH-500 per-problem rows, real Modal CPU jobs, private boards.
Plants named per review: skill 3.1, plain 2.6. Plants left of 6 after round 3: skill 2/3/3, plain 4/4/2. No removed plant came back.
Against the skill: on clean work both skill reviews cut the bootstrap from 1.5M resamples to 10-20k against a written owner requirement (same point estimates, interval ends moved up to 1.9% of the width, 7x less compute); plain reviews left the answers alone. No review of 18 named the cell whose answer was already stored; the skill named the off-mission benchmark in 8 of 9 reviews and removed it in none.
Limits: scripted worker, n=3 per arm, no test; best plain run is 2 points from the worst skill run.
Bug in shared code: tools/gpu.py state() reports a running job as 'died: ConnectionError: Deadline exceeded' when Modal's API call fails; a retry fixes it (studies/metaharness/lib/arena.py patch_gpu_state).

RL does not win by checking more: it writes more checking markers (13.1 vs 9.5 per 1k tokens, paired +3.6 [3.4, 3.9], n=500, all of it wait/hmm/actually), but markers do not separate right from wrong samples of the same model and problem (base right minus wrong +0.63 [-0.01, 1.28] per 1k, +0.08 [-0.64, 0.77] at matched length, 150 problems; RL wrong samples have more), the rate after 52 located base wrong steps equals that of right siblings (9.2 vs 9.2; a marker within 500 tokens after 88 % of steps vs 87 % at random positions), and blind judges call 5 of 80 check events a fix (base 3 of 40, RL 2 of 40; kappa 0.88, planted controls 20 of 20 and 19 of 20). 6 of 11 base slips read are followed by a check that repeats the slip. What differs: first wrong steps per 1k finished tokens, 0.015 RL vs 0.038 base. Not separable at 40 events per model: fewer errors made vs a larger share caught. Judges are the agent's own subagents. Prediction filed on work-74703c: Wait steering changes the cued base by 0 points [-2, +1]. studies/rlneurons/results/checks/math500-01/ and judge-01/, README section 'Checks or per-step error', commit adafdc5.

Steering dose run (SPEC3, work-74703c): adding the J-lens direction of Wait/Hmm to one block of the cued base during generation raises written hold-on words steeply and specifically. 63 MATH-500 problems, cap 1,024 tokens, T 1.0. Hold-on words per 1,000 tokens: none 6.53; layer 24 at alpha 0.03 / 0.06 / 0.12 / 0.25 (share of the block's median output norm): 7.37 / 8.09 / 15.9 / 92.5 (repeated 'wait'); layer 20 at 0.06 / 0.12 / 0.25: 7.19 / 8.52 / 20.8; random direction of equal norm at layer 24, alpha 0.12: 6.47 (ratio 0.99); logit bias on the six tokens 0.5 / 1 / 2 nats: 8.77 / 10.0 / 26.7. Strengths that give the RL model's ratio 1.41 (8.81 vs 6.24 per 1,000 in stored T2 vs T1): alpha 0.068 at layer 24, 0.128 at layer 20, bias 0.64 nats. Method note: the hook runs inside vLLM 0.32 (in-process engine, enforce_eager, no prefix cache), 11 minutes for 17 arms. No accuracy yet: the main run (500 problems, cap 16,384, 5 jobs) is running. studies/jspace/results/steer/dose-01/metrics.json, branch claude/wait-steering-f535b2 1534ce9.

Activation edits during generation run inside vLLM 0.32 at vLLM speed, no Hugging Face generate needed. vLLM serves Olmo 3 through its Transformers backend, so model.model.layers[l] are the Hugging Face blocks and a torch forward hook on a block acts on every sequence of the batch (hidden state [1, tokens of all running requests, 4096]). Needed: VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 (model in the job's process), EngineArgs(enforce_eager=True) (a Python hook is not replayed by a CUDA graph), enable_prefix_caching=False when arms differ in activations; find the model by walking the engine's attributes (vLLM freezes the gc list). Per-request logit_bias works with seeded sampling. Instrument check to copy: a huge edit must change every answer (alpha 8 gave only 'wait' tokens). Measured: 17 arms x 63 problems x 1,024 tokens in 11 minutes on one H100; a 500-problem arm at cap 16,384 in 31 to 35 minutes, the same as run_cell; a random direction of 6.8 % of the block norm scores 409/500 (stored unsteered cells 404 to 418). Code: studies/jspace/jobs/steer_gen.py (Engine, find_model, Hook), branch claude/wait-steering-f535b2.

Negative: the cued base's activations do not tell which of its own samples of a problem will fail. MATH-500, 2,000 stored samples (4 per problem, T 1.0, v3), linear probe on the residual stream (layers 12/20/28) after 250/500/1,000/2,000 answer tokens, 5 folds by problem, target with no answer key (sample is in the largest group of agreeing answers). Within-problem AUROC (good vs bad sample of the same problem, 110-137 problems): 0.51 / 0.54 / 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] / 0.51; the same probe trained on the answer key 0.51-0.55; mean log-prob and entropy so far 0.49-0.57. Across problems the probe at the last prompt token predicts the flag at 0.73-0.77: the base encodes how hard the problem is before writing, not which sample goes wrong. Offline stop-and-restart at 1,000 tokens with the probe: 414.1/500 at 4,345 tokens vs one sample 410.5 at 4,008; probe minus random-score +0.8 pts [-0.7, 2.4]. Ceiling with a perfect critic at 1,000 tokens: 438.7 (no key) and 459.2 (key) at about 4,100 tokens, RL single 456. C1-C3 refuted. Checks: exactly 0.500 at the prompt position, 0.49-0.50 with flags shuffled within problems, planted signal found. Limits: linear, one position, 3 layers, n 2,000; a critic that reads the finished answer was not tested. Note for anyone voting on stored rows: comparing extracted_v3 strings splits equal answers (39 % of problems look unanimous); group with rln4_lib.agree. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/critic/{ceiling-02,probe-02}/metrics.json, README section 'Critic at decoding time', branch critic. About 2 USD.

Slip-hazard law refuted: the hazard (cloglog) item model fits held-out cells worse than Rasch logit, -0.2854 vs -0.2790 nats per cell (T -0.0064, all 5 folds; logit-simulated null -0.0026 [-0.0048, -0.0010], hazard-simulated +0.0031; power 1.0 both ways), 36 arms x 500 MATH-500 problems. RL's hazard ratio is not constant: 0.48 on the hardest 46 problems, 0.23 on the middle 119, 0.11 on the easiest 335 (base wrong cells 157/130/71, RL 117/35/8; hardest minus easiest -1.47 on the log scale, constant-ratio range -0.55 to +0.30). Average hazard ratios vs pooled base + cue: RL plain 0.33 [0.28, 0.40], RL cue 0.37, Think-SFT 0.37, Code-RL 0.44, theta 0.25/0.5/0.75 0.56/0.43/0.43 (log hazard not linear in theta: theta 0.25 has 57 %), base vote over 4 0.51, RL vote over 4 0.60 vs its own samples. Transfer to hard328 (5 arms): same hazard ratio 5.11 problems, calibrated hazard 8.03, point 5.14, logit 5.07: no better than point. Fitted work rises with right-answer tokens (Spearman 0.48 base, 0.59 RL, shuffled +/-0.09) but with slope 0.45 and 0.77, not 1. 4-sample outcomes: bulk variance binomial (D 1.03, 0.90; null 95th pct 1.17), but 8 (base) and 12 (RL) more 0-of-4 problems than binomial and the vote 10 and 9 problems below the independent-slip prediction. Post hoc: the data lie past logit on the side away from the hazard link. Hazard predictions for 5 running cells filed in commit 1da4655 (none finished yet). studies/rlneurons/results/hazard/math500-01/readout.json, table.md; transfer-01/, predict-01/, scored-01/; README section 'Slip-hazard law'; spec specs/SPEC_hazard.md

Negative: forcing the cued base to commit when an answer runs long loses problems; its cap hits on the 328 are failures to solve, not failures to stop. Stored T 1.0 answers cut at N tokens + commit line, only the continuation graded (v3). Configuration chosen on MATH-500 by the pre-written rule: forced box at N 8,000 (MATH-500 406 vs 405 stored). Headline on hard328: 152/328 vs 164 stored, -3.7 pts [-6.4, -1.2], at 6,017 vs 9,344 generated tokens per problem. All six on the 328: N 4,000 box 130, voice 126; N 8,000 box 152, voice 151; N 12,000 box 159 (-1.5 [-4.0, 0.9], 7,927 tokens), voice 158. Of the 77 stored cap hits a forced commit is right on 0-2 at every N. Of the 184 answers over 8,000 tokens, 28 are right when forced, 40 when left alone; the commit keeps 24 of those 40. A sentence in the answer's own voice is never better than the forced box. This scores the open arm C of RLN-3 (knowledge-0b450e). H1, H2 refuted, H3 at the edge (SPEC_commit1.md). Hand read of 14 forced boxes: 4 right, 10 guesses. RL not run (only if H1 held). Use: do not spend a cell on budget forcing or early stop for the 328; the tokens between 8,000 and 16,384 buy 12 problems. 1,656 requests, 8 min on one H100. Loop neurons, rerun on all 68 loops of base+cue MATH-500 T 0.6 (34 rank, 34 held out, teacher-forced continuation 1,600 tokens): zeroing 100 neurons ranked by effect leaves 1/34 loops (unedited 19/34; 100 random 19/34; 1,000 by effect 0/34; 1,000 random 15 and 18/34), normal-text loss +5.0 %. Dose on the first 1,000 (14 rows): activations x0, x0.5, x1, x2 give 1, 1, 3, 8 loops; 1,000 random x0, x2 give 3, 3. Their activations deviate from normal text before the onset (mean |z| 0.17 at -200..-50 tokens vs 0.08 random) and rise through the loop (0.38 in cycle 2). Published: a repetition penalty removes loops without MATH-500 gain (arXiv 2610.24715 Table 16), as our zeroing did (result-6de887). Artifacts: studies/cleanneurons/results/loops/real-02/metrics.json, results/describe/attr1000_loops-01/{metrics,dose_summary,onset_summary}.json, branch claude/clean-neuron-hypothesis-9e2ed3 79fa896. Math-RL is about half as likely as the base to write the base's own located wrong step, and the base's wrong step is not an unlikely sample. 51 judged finished-wrong samples of the cued base (MATH-500; first wrong step located, median 29 tokens), D = (log p_model - log p_base) over the step minus the same over 200 control spans of the same answer, nats [95 %]: Mix 3.0 -0.80 [-1.34, -0.28], Math 3.1 -0.71 [-1.48, 0.01] (factor 0.49; measured ratio of first wrong steps 0.39, result-855858), Math 3.0 -0.58, Code 3.1 -0.45 [-0.79, -0.12], Code 3.0 -0.32 [-0.95, 0.27], General -0.14, theta(0.25) -0.10, random difference 0.00 [-0.02, 0.02], IF +0.17. Order follows the cue gain of result-edceef (Spearman -0.67, n 9). By label for Math 3.1: misread -1.52, slip -0.72, wrong plan +0.03: RL lowers misreadings and slips, not wrong plans. Under the base the wrong step has log-prob -0.53 per token vs -0.63 for control text (W4 refuted): truncation or low temperature cannot remove these steps, which fits the min-p/top-p negatives. W1 not met as written (interval touches 0; the effect is in a minority of items, median -0.26), W2, W3 held. Limits: 51 items, judges are our subagents. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/math500-01/{metrics,items}.json, README section 'Wrong steps', branch critic. About 3 USD.

Think-SFT and RL have different difficulty profiles, and the blind prediction from that held on hard328: Think-SFT cue 219/328 (profile rule 217.6; one-axis rules Lc 196.3, P 190.5; RL 205-206), plain 203 (Lc 183.2, profile 218.3). MATH-500, n=500, 1 Think-SFT sample vs 4 RL: contrast C = -1.54 by MATH level (one-axis range -0.89..+0.83, same-arm max 0.61), mostly the easy side: levels 1-2 Think-SFT 10 wrong vs RL 2.0 and base 8.5 (z 3.7); level 5 23 vs 25.5 (z -1.5, noise). 24 of its 46 errors are cap hits (RL 18 %). 2PL beats Rasch held out (+0.0039 nats/cell, null max -0.0001) but separates plain-prompt arms and Think-SFT from the rest, not SFT from RL. Union with one RL sample +2.8 problems over two RL samples: not complementary on MATH-500. Not controlled: overlap of the 328 with Think-SFT training data (result-d9d6f3); hard328 counts read from the board, Think-SFT raw text not readable (other workspace). Stack for the lead (not run): Think-SFT + 1.0 (RL - base), cue, MATH-500 + hard328, ~1.5 H100 h; additive predicts 467/500, <=460 refutes. xreward Part 2, first four cells (hard328 n=328, cue, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, one sample, seed 3000000; edits at 0.074 % of weight norm): the 8 directions and the rest of the RL difference each carry about two thirds of the hard-problem gain, by different routes. Right of 328 and cap hits: base 164, 77; matched random rank-8 158, 67; base + Math 3.1 top-8 directions per matrix 192, 46; Math 3.1 minus those 8 directions 190, 90; RL 206, 20; base + Code 3.1 top-8 178, 41. Negative: giving the cued base the RL model's Wait habit does not raise MATH-500 (SPEC3, idea-da9dca, work-74703c). The J-lens direction of Wait/Hmm added to layer 24 during generation until the base writes them at the RL model's rate (8.32 per 1,000 tokens; RL 8.81; unsteered 6.28): 413/500, n=500, T 1.0, cap 16,384, v3. Against four stored unsteered samples (mean 410.5): +0.5 pts [-2.2, +3.1]; against a random direction of the same norm (409): +0.8 [-2.6, +4.2]; RL is 457. Stronger push (alpha 0.1, 11.2 per 1,000): 381, -5.9 [-9.0, -2.9]; 39 answers end without an answer (unsteered 5). Same written rate from layer 20: 398. Logit bias on the six tokens (0.64 nats, 9.72 per 1,000): 421, not below the push (push minus bias -1.6 [-5.0, +1.8]), so the workspace adds nothing over a decoding bias. Why: (1) the push adds the word without a check: a blind reader labelled 16 of 20 push-inserted Waits as filler, 1 as a fix; of the model's own Waits 7 of 20 are fixes; (2) on the 65 problems T1 missed and T2 solved: unsteered 42, random 35, push 35; (3) inside, the push overshoots: hold-on words in the layer-24 readout at 31 % of positions, vs 4.75 % unsteered and 6.29 % in RL; alpha 0.017 already gives 7.2 %. The readout difference is a trace of the habit, not its cause. Caveat: my unsteered arm scored 430 (above the stored 404-418; same sampling path, 48 texts identical to T1); read as a high draw, second seed running. One sample per arm, SD about 7 problems. studies/jspace/results/steer/main-01/metrics.json, readout-01/readout.json, README 'SPEC 3', branch claude/wait-steering-f535b2 1cc3ac8.
